summary.text: Doris Matsui is the Democratic incumbent for California's 7th Congressional District. Born in the Poston, Arizona internment camp, she worked in the Clinton White House before winning a 2005 special election to succeed her late husband, Rep. Bob Matsui. She serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

paragraphs.text: Matsui was born in Poston, Arizona, in 1944, and grew up on a farm in California's Central Valley; Wikipedia gives her birth name as Doris Okada and says she grew up in Dinuba.
She graduated from the University of California, Berkeley, earning a B.A. in 1966 (a psychology degree, according to Wikipedia), and met her husband, Bob Matsui, while at Berkeley.

Matsui volunteered on Bill Clinton's 1992 presidential campaign and served on the Clinton-Gore transition team, which her official biography describes as one of eight members of the transition board, then worked in the White House Office of Public Liaison from 1993 to 1998, including as deputy director.

President Clinton appointed her to the board of the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars in 2000, and Wikipedia reports she then worked as a Washington lobbyist for corporate clients until 2005.
She also chaired the board of the KVIE public television station in Sacramento before entering Congress.
Her husband, Rep. Bob Matsui, who served in Congress from 1979 to 2005, died on January 1, 2005.

Doris Matsui won the March 8, 2005 special election to succeed him in what was then California's 5th District and has been re-elected since 2006; the district number changed to the 6th in 2013 and the 7th in 2023.

She serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, including its Communications and Technology and Energy subcommittees (2025-2026); Ballotpedia lists her as ranking member of the Communications and Technology Subcommittee in 2023-2024, and her official biography describes her as its ranking member.
She chaired the Democratic Women's Working Group from 2015 to 2017, and has served on the Smithsonian Board of Regents.
Her official biography says she has secured over $4 billion in federal investment for local flood prevention and that she authored the CHIPS for America Act.
Matsui married AES Corporation co-founder Roger Sant in 2020, according to Wikipedia and her official biography; she has a son, Brian.
